Make an example single-cell dataset with multiple exposures

Source: R/make_example_data.R
make_example_sc.Rd

Creates a sample SingleCellExperiment object with sample-level exposures (two continuous, one binary, plus age), cell types, and negative binomial counts. A subset of genes truly responds to each exposure, and some exposures act only in specific cell types. The true effect sizes are stored in rowData() so results can be benchmarked.

Usage

make_example_sc(
  n_samples = 12,
  cells_per_sample = 200,
  n_genes = 1000,
  n_celltypes = 4,
  prop_responsive = 0.08,
  effect_sd = 0.6,
  prop_celltype_responsive = 0.6,
  size = 2
)

Arguments

n_samples

Number of samples (donors).

cells_per_sample

Number of cells simulated per sample.

n_genes

Number of genes.

n_celltypes

Number of cell types (named CT1, CT2, ...).

prop_responsive

Proportion of genes with a true effect for each exposure.

effect_sd

Standard deviation of the true (log-scale) exposure effects.

prop_celltype_responsive

Probability that a cell type responds to a given exposure. CT1 always responds to every exposure.

size

Negative binomial size (dispersion) parameter. Smaller values give more overdispersion.

Value

A SingleCellExperiment with:

assays$counts

Genes x cells count matrix.

colData

sample, pm25, bpa, smoker, age, celltype.

rowData

beta_pm25, beta_bpa, beta_smoker: true effects, where nonzero means a truly responsive gene.

metadata$responsive

Cell type x exposure matrix of which cell types respond to which exposures.

Details

Exposures are constant within a sample, so the effective sample size is the number of samples, not the number of cells.

Examples

sce <- make_example_sc()
